description: The one case table for a company name's display casing, run by both copies of the rule: frontend/lib/formatCompanyName.ts (frontend/tests/unit/formatCompanyName.spec.ts) and backend/app/utils/company_names.py (backend/tests/unit/test_company_names.py). Each group names the part of the rule its cases pin; each case is [served name, display name].

groups.why: ALL-CAPS EDGAR names are title-cased per token with a small exceptions list.

groups.rule: cases the body when only the legal suffix is cased
groups.why: Live sec.gov company_tickers.json: ~1,300-1,600 of 10,412 titles are ALL CAPS except the legal suffix. A cased suffix must not exempt the shouting body in front of it.

groups.rule: cases a legal form before its marker and keeps the marker
groups.why: Chief design on #1491 (6347648492): a legal form with EDGAR's marker glued on reads as the same legal form without one; the marker keeps its capitals, and a marker alone stays as served. Only letter case changes.

groups.rule: keeps a trailing group of tickers as served
groups.why: EDGAR's full-text search folds every ticker of a multi-class or warrant-carrying filer into its display name; the group is data, so it stays as served (the review of #1491, measured on live display names).

groups.rule: resolves initialisms and overrides through glued punctuation
keeps legal-form and brand initialisms upper-case
lower-cases connectives mid-name but not when they lead
cases hyphen, apostrophe and dotted segments individually
cases the letters of any script
groups.why: Codex on #1491: a letter is any script's, with its accents, so an accented capital stays inside its word (a decomposed accent too), a word is lowercased whole (a Greek final sigma keeps its form) with its first letter's own capital, a name cased in another script is trusted, and a script without case is left as served.

groups.rule: applies brand overrides and preserves tokens with digits or ampersands
normalises whitespace and reads an empty name as empty
reads space and lowercase as JavaScript does
groups.why: The Python copy's own pitfalls: trim() strips a byte-order mark, which str.strip() keeps, and \p{Ll} is general category Ll, while str.islower() also counts Other_Lowercase letters such as the ordinal ª.
